findings.title: A channel is stored as active and submit reports success before the counterparty has acknowledged
findings.source: live runs: omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs against Hawk v0.2.12 and v0.3.0
findings.summary: submitOpenChannel writes the channel into the local store as active, then asks the peer. When the peer rejects, the store is not rolled back and the response is still { success: true, acknowledged: false }. The local node therefore reports a live channel that the counterparty has no record of.
findings.impact: Funds are committed to a 2-of-2 output whose other party will not co-sign, so the value is unusable until the counterparty is made aware. Any router or UI that reads channel state sees an active channel and will attempt payments that cannot settle. acknowledged=false is easy to ignore and is not reflected in status.

repro.expected: Either the channel is not persisted as active until the ACK arrives, or the failure is recorded on the channel (for example status "pending-ack") and the RPC reports failure.
repro.actual: totem_omniaGetChannelState on the initiator returns status "active" with totalValue 100000000 for channel 0x8e3aac4a4d94b3b45ae5dc4f7317e7ea, while the responder returns "Channel ... not found"; submit returned success:true, acknowledged:false.
evidence: initiator A: totem_omniaGetChannelState -> status "active", channelId 0x8e3aac4a4d94b3b45ae5dc4f7317e7ea
responder B: totem_omniaGetChannelState -> error "Channel 0x8e3aac4a4d94b3b45ae5dc4f7317e7ea not found"
submit response: {"success":true,"acknowledged":false,"fundingTxId":"0x000101961A785E7B2724D42ADAB585B2CF66487E96A3E6950396E881DA16BD57"}
the funding output is on chain and unspent, held by MULTISIG(2, A, B)
0.3.0: initiator reported status "active" for channel 0xe6863650602f6f7a3e1b99df1ebba8d1 while the responder returned "not found"
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts: channels.set(...) happens before requestPeerReply, with no rollback on non-ACK

fix.approach: Make the persisted status reflect what was agreed. Keep the on-chain funding fact, but mark the channel pending acknowledgment until the peer ACKs, and return a non-success result (or an explicit partial result) when the peer rejects. If the channel is left in pending-ack, give it a documented recovery path that re-sends the proposal once the funding coin is visible.
constraints: Do not hide the on-chain funding output; its existence is still true and needed for recovery.
Do not make the ACK authoritative for the on-chain state (the tx is already posted).
Do not change the funding script or state contract.
acceptance: A rejected open is not reported as an active channel by the initiator.
The initiator exposes a recoverable pending-ack channel that can be re-proposed and becomes active once the peer ACKs.
A normal open still results in status active only after the ACK.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 44-omnia-noncustodial-live  # responder must report the same channel

findings.title: Unsolicited SPLICE_FINALIZED and VC_FINALIZED messages overwrite trusted channel state
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-001, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: The SPLICE_FINALIZED handler takes payload.channel from the peer message and writes it straight into the channel store. The VC_FINALIZED handler does the same for payload.factory and payload.channel, and deletes a channel on vc-close. Neither handler checks that the sender is the expected counterparty, that a proposal or acceptance is outstanding for that id, that the payload carries valid signatures, or that any chain evidence supports it.
findings.impact: Any connected peer can overwrite persisted channel or factory state with its own object, or make the host forget a channel. Exploitability depends on transport access control: peers are bound by their transport key from the DHT and there is no allowlist, so "connected" is the only bar. This is a source-level finding; no exploit was executed.

repro.expected: A finalized message that does not match a locally recorded proposal/acceptance is rejected, and state is only written after signature and chain verification.
repro.actual: lifecycle.ts writes the peer-supplied object unconditionally: channelStore.set on SPLICE_FINALIZED, and factory/channel set plus channelStore.delete on VC_FINALIZED.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (peer-guards.assertSpliceFinalized / assertVcFinalized); 19 guard tests
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:365 — if (msg.type === "SPLICE_FINALIZED" && payload.channel) channelStore.set(...)
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:588 — VC_FINALIZED: factories.set(payload.factory) and channelStore.set/delete(payload.channel)
no lookup of spliceAcceptances/vcReplies before either write

fix.approach: Treat a finalized message as a claim, not a fact. Require an outstanding local record keyed by spliceId or vcId, verify the finalized payload against that proposal (parties, balances, sequence, successor coin) and verify the counterparty signatures, then persist. Reject unsolicited ids instead of applying them.
constraints: Do not trust any object supplied by the peer as authoritative state.
Do not break the legitimate finalize path after a local acceptance.
Keep emitting the existing observation events on success.
acceptance: A SPLICE_FINALIZED with no matching local acceptance is rejected and changes nothing.
A VC_FINALIZED cannot delete a channel that has no outstanding close acceptance.
A legitimate finalize still persists and becomes active.

findings.title: FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST signs an arbitrary peer-supplied digest
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-004, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: The FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST handler takes payload.digest, reserves a WOTS leaf, signs those exact bytes and returns the signature. It does not require an authorized pending factory, does not verify the proposed transaction, and does not bind the digest to a funding coin or to a locally initiated funding round. The host signs with the same tree it uses for other operations.
findings.impact: A connected peer can use the host as a signing oracle: any 32-byte digest it chooses gets a valid WOTS signature, consuming key material. Whether a returned signature can authorize a malicious on-chain spend was not demonstrated end to end; the missing binding is the defect either way.

repro.expected: A funding signature is produced only for a digest the host derived itself for a funding round it is part of.
repro.actual: The handler signs payload.digest after only checking that a local bundle exists.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (resolveFactoryFundingTarget binds the digest to an accepted factory and a participant peer)
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:394 — onFactoryMessage returns early only if !factories || !localBundle
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:410 — digest parsed from payload.digest
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:418 — localBundle.signer.sign(digest, reservation.indices)

fix.approach: Derive the digest locally from the pending factory proposal and funding coin, compare it to the request, and sign only on a match. Require an outstanding funding round with a known counterparty. Never sign an opaque digest supplied by a peer.
constraints: Do not keep an arbitrary-digest path behind a flag.
Do not reserve a leaf before the digest is validated (a rejected request must not burn key material).
acceptance: A request whose digest does not match the locally computed funding digest is rejected without reserving a leaf.
A request with no outstanding funding round is rejected.
The legitimate round still produces a valid signature.

findings.title: Factory proposal still signs a peer-controlled commitment
findings.source: re-audit R-001, verified against source at 5d8c427b
findings.summary: CAN-010 closed the FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST oracle by binding the digest to an accepted factory, but a second signing path remains. FACTORY_PROPOSAL carries a peer-supplied ChannelFactory; the host calls acceptFactory(factory), which converts factory.pendingCommitment to bytes and signs it. Nothing reconstructs the funding transaction or checks that the commitment is what this participant agreed to fund.
findings.impact: A peer that can submit a proposal naming the local signer can solicit a WOTS signature over an attacker-chosen commitment. That signature is a factory funding witness, so it is the material that authorises spending the participant coin. Source-level finding; no exploit executed.

repro.expected: The commitment is derived locally from validated factory terms and funding transaction bytes; a proposal whose commitment does not match is rejected before a leaf is reserved.
repro.actual: acceptFactory signs factory.pendingCommitment exactly as supplied in the proposal.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #222: proposal carries funding materials; the acceptor rebuilds the funding tx and signs only the derived commitment
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:462 — FACTORY_PROPOSAL calls acceptFactory(payload.factory, localBundle)
packages/omnia-factory/src/factory.ts:502 — acceptFactory takes factory.pendingCommitment
packages/omnia-factory/src/factory.ts:517 — Buffer.from(factory.pendingCommitment, "hex") is signed by leaseSign
no reconstruction of the funding draft in the accept path

fix.approach: Make the acceptor derive the commitment: rebuild the funding transaction from the proposal terms and funding materials with buildFactoryOpening, compare its pendingCommitment to the proposal, and sign only the locally derived value. Require the proposal to carry the funding materials it was built from.
constraints: Do not sign a commitment that is only peer-supplied.
Do not reserve a WOTS leaf before the commitment is verified.
Keep the legitimate single-proposer flow working end to end.
acceptance: A proposal whose commitment differs from the locally rebuilt funding transaction is rejected.
A legitimate proposal still produces an accepted factory with both opening signatures.
Covered by a two-host prepare → sign → finalize test.

findings.title: Peer-scoped finalization stores peer-supplied factory, channel and splice state
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-001
findings.summary: FACTORY_FINALIZED opening→active is validated, but two branches are not: active→active returns the incoming object wholesale, and opening→opening accepts additional pending signatures without verifying them. In the host, VC_FINALIZED writes `payload.factory` to the factory store after checking only factoryId and sequence+1, SPLICE_FINALIZED writes `payload.channel` after binding checks that never recompute balances or signatures, and FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED marks a known factory closed without any settlement evidence.
findings.impact: A participant (or a compromised peer) can replace another participant's locally accepted factory state, channel state or closure status. Fund loss requires a downstream path that trusts the stored object; inconsistent accounting and stuck funds are reachable without one.

repro.expected: Every peer finalization message is rejected unless the resulting state can be rebuilt from local state plus a transition that verifies.
repro.actual: assertFactoryFinalized returns `{...incoming}` for active→active, and lifecycle.ts stores `payload.factory` and `payload.channel` after identity/sequence checks only.
evidence: packages/omnia-factory/src/factory.ts: assertFactoryFinalized active→active and opening→opening branches
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts: `factories.set(payload.factory.factoryId, payload.factory)`
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts: `channelStore.set(channel.channelId, channel)` for SPLICE_FINALIZED
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts: FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED sets status closed unconditionally

fix.approach: Derive the expected object locally for every finalization message: rebuild the factory/channel transition from the local copy, verify every participant signature and the state commitment, then store the rebuilt object rather than the peer payload. Reject unknown added signatures. Require a settlement artifact bound to the factory before accepting a close.
constraints: Do not accept a whole replacement object from a peer on any message type.
Do not weaken the opening→active checks that already exist.
Keep the wire format unchanged; this is a validation-boundary fix.
A rejected message must leave the store byte-identical.
acceptance: A matrix test covers every peer finalization handler against sequence, allocation, signature, identity and replay mutations; every case is rejected and the store is unchanged.
Factory active→active validates sequence progression and the state log before storing.
Opening→opening verifies any signature it did not already hold.
FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED requires finality evidence bound to the factory id and settlement.
The valid-path cases still succeed.

origin.note: Aliased to CAN-019, which tracks identifier-only finalization guards. CAN-007 covers the unsolicited-message half; this entry adds the factory active→active / opening→opening branches.

findings.title: A transferred VTXO keeps the previous owner's exit entitlement
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-003
findings.summary: transferVtxo verifies `params.exitEntitlement` against the input VTXO, then copies the same object onto the output VTXO, whose owner and vtxoId are both new. verifyVtxoExitEntitlement binds owner, vtxoId, amount and holderIndex, so the attached artifact cannot verify for the recipient — and the exit transaction pays the previous owner. The entitlement is also optional, so a transfer may attach none at all.
findings.impact: A recipient receives a VTXO with an exit that pays the sender, or no exit. Any consumer that treats the presence of `exitEntitlement` as proof of a recipient-executable exit can lose the value.

repro.expected: verifyVtxoExitEntitlement(outputVtxo, outputVtxo.exitEntitlement).valid === true after a transfer.
repro.actual: The entitlement still names the input owner/vtxoId, so verification against the output fails on vtxoId, owner and holderIndex.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/transfer.ts: verify against `vtxo`, then spread `params.exitEntitlement` onto `outputVtxo`
packages/omnia-vtxo/src/exit-entitlement.ts: verify checks vtxoId, owner, amount, holderIndex
packages/omnia-vtxo/src/exit-tx.ts: output 0 pays `wotsAddressData(params.vtxo.owner)`

fix.approach: Build the recipient's exit from the output VTXO (recipient as holderIndex owner, output id, same amount) and verify it before returning. Either require an exit for a full transfer or make the absence explicit in the result so callers cannot mistake it for an executable claim.
constraints: Do not mutate the input entitlement into the output; rebuild it.
Partial transfers must not inherit an entitlement.
The exit transaction must still spend the same pool coin and preserve the remainder output.
acceptance: A two-owner transfer produces an entitlement that verifies against the output.
A transfer without an entitlement reports that explicitly and is never described as exit-ready.
A partial transfer cannot carry an exit entitlement.

findings.title: Vesting policy never enforces the vested amount before the end block
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-008
findings.summary: The vesting case checks the cliff, then `if (ctx.block >= endBlock) return valid`; before the end block it computes `elapsed` and `span` and never uses them, returning valid for any positive `claimAmount`. The maximum vested amount at the current block is therefore never enforced.
findings.impact: A beneficiary can claim the entire vesting allocation immediately after the cliff. This is direct value loss for any VTXO using the vesting policy.

repro.expected: At block `< endBlock`, a claim above the linear vested amount is rejected.
repro.actual: Any `claimAmount > 0` is accepted once the cliff is reached.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/claim-policy.ts: vesting branch returns `total > 0n ? {valid:true} : …`
packages/omnia-vtxo/src/claim-policy.ts: `elapsed`/`span` computed but unused

fix.approach: Compute the vested amount as a function of block (`cliff`, `startBlock`, `endBlock`) and reject a claim above it; use the elapsed/span values that are already derived. Make the cliff and end blocks explicit in the result so callers can display the schedule.
constraints: Do not remove the cliff check.
Partial claims before the end block must remain possible up to the vested amount.
Do not change the policy shape without a migration note.
acceptance: A claim above the vested amount at the current block is rejected.
A claim at or below the vested amount succeeds.
At/after endBlock the full amount is claimable.

findings.title: Channel funding draft silently drops the unspent part of the funding coin
findings.source: artifacts/canary/src/composition/__tests__/CrossPackage.test.ts
findings.summary: buildFundingTx takes explicit input amounts but always emits exactly one output (the channel coin). It neither returns change nor checks that inputs cover outputs, and buildChannelOpening passes the whole funding coin. Opening a channel from a coin larger than localAmount + remoteAmount therefore produces a draft whose inputs exceed its outputs by the unspent remainder. tx-builder buildTransaction does not check conservation either, so nothing fails until a node rejects the unbalanced transaction.
findings.impact: Reachable from the RPC surface: omnia-host forwards fundingCoinId unchanged, so any wallet that does not pre-select an exactly-sized coin fails to open a channel with an opaque node rejection. No funds are lost (the node refuses the transaction) but the failure is late and misattributed.

repro.expected: The draft either pays the remainder back to the funding coin address (change output) or throws when sum(inputs) > totalValue.
repro.actual: The draft contains a single output. inputs sum 1500 while outputs sum 1000, and no layer rejects it. Recorded as a node:test TODO so it stays visible without failing the gate.
evidence: CANARY FINDING: an over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected (TODO)
packages/omnia/src/transactions.ts: buildFundingTx
packages/omnia/src/channel.ts: buildChannelOpening passes fundingCoin.amount as the input
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts: prepareOpenChannel forwards fundingCoinId
packages/tx-builder/src/build.ts: buildTransaction has no conservation check

fix.approach: Add a change output to the input coin address in buildFundingTx when sum(inputs) > totalValue, or reject the draft with a clear error. Do both at the right layers: omnia owns channel funding semantics, tx-builder should refuse to serialise an unbalanced transaction rather than deferring to the node.
constraints: Do not change the funding output state contract: STATE(100)=false, STATE(101)=0.
Do not change computeOmniaTxDigest / canonical byte semantics.
Do not mask this in the canary, in omnia-host, or with a coin pre-selection workaround.
Keep the single-input fast path byte-identical when the input equals totalValue.
acceptance: buildFundingTx returns a change output to the funding coin address when inputs exceed totalValue.
buildFundingTx (or buildChannelOpening) throws when inputs are less than totalValue.
tx-builder buildTransaction rejects a draft whose input sum is below its output sum.
Unit tests cover over-funded, exact, and under-funded inputs.
The canary test "over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected" is un-TODOed and passes.

findings.title: Manifest proofs are not bound to the manifest they attest
findings.source: artifacts/canary/src/composition/__tests__/ProofAndMoney.test.ts
findings.summary: verifyManifestProof verifies the manifest signature and the proof envelope independently and never compares them. A proof whose payload.manifestId names a different manifest, a proof of a different kind (attestation), and a proof issued by an unrelated key all verify as valid against any correctly signed manifest.
findings.impact: An attestation issued for one manifest can be presented as attestation for another (for example a later version with the same appId), and a non-manifest proof can be passed off as a manifest attestation. Verifiers that rely on the pairing will over-report assurance.

repro.expected: A proof for manifest A is rejected against manifest B, a non-manifest proof is rejected, and a foreign issuer is rejected.
repro.actual: All three return valid: true, because verifyManifestProof never reads proof.payload, proof.kind or the proof issuer relative to the manifest.
evidence: packages/proof/src/manifest-proof.ts: verifyManifestProof = verifyManifest(signedManifest) then verifyProof(signedProof)
createManifestProof stores payload { manifestId } from the caller, and nothing compares it back
canary observed: proof for A vs manifest B -> valid; attestation proof vs manifest A -> valid; proof with unrelated manifestId -> valid; proof from a third-party issuer -> valid

fix.approach: Bind the pair explicitly: require proof.kind === 'manifest', require the proof issuer to be the manifest author address, and compare payload.manifestId with the identifier computed from the supplied manifest. Decide and document which identifier that is (content digest via computeManifestId is the strongest; appId is weaker and would still allow version substitution), then make createManifestProof derive it from the SignedManifest rather than trusting a caller string.
constraints: Do not change the manifest signing format or computeManifestId semantics.
Do not accept a wildcard or "any" manifestId to preserve callers.
Keep verifyManifest false-paths and reasons unchanged.
acceptance: verifyManifestProof rejects a proof issued for a different manifest (version substitution).
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose kind is not manifest.
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose issuer does not match the manifest author.
The honest proof/manifest pair still verifies.
The canary TODO test flips to a normal passing test.

findings.title: Non-custodial channel open races the chain: the acceptor validates the funding coin before it can be mined
findings.source: live runs: omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs against Hawk v0.2.12 and v0.3.0 (us-east-1 hosts A/B)
findings.summary: SubmitOpenChannel posts the funding transaction and, in the same call, sends CHANNEL_PROPOSAL to the counterparty. The responder's acceptChannel requires the funding coin to already exist on chain and throws "Funding coin <id> not found on chain". On a real node the transaction cannot be included in a block in the microseconds between the post and the proposal, so a first-time open always fails. The initiator does not wait for inclusion, and the responder does not wait or retry.
findings.impact: Every two-party channel open against a live node fails at the peer handshake, even though the funding transaction is valid and is mined moments later. Offline and in-memory suites do not catch it because their chain view already contains the coin when the proposal is handled. This blocks every channel-based use case from being opened on a real network.

repro.expected: The responder accepts the proposal and reports status "active" for the channel.
repro.actual: Submit returns success with acknowledged=false; the responder answers CHANNEL_PROPOSAL with ERROR "acceptChannel failed: Error: Funding coin <id> not found on chain"; the status poll on the responder never finds the channel.
evidence: live invocation: NODE=http://127.0.0.1:9005 HOST_B=http://172.31.74.14:50056/rpc WALLET=http://127.0.0.1:51060 FUNDING_COIN_ID=<confirmed 2e8 coin> REMOTE_TRANSPORT=<b transport> LOCAL_AMOUNT=60000000 REMOTE_AMOUNT=40000000 node scripts/omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs

channel 0xc31032e2ab44dcaf9bc0a60287a1725b: rejected coin 0x68778de3fa2b6819865ec98405849cfb5e1ca3a042472e6f9767bdd47e4f4d27
funding tx 0x00012CD06D63AF0F7ED60A4915381BF30D0E8A4FB93647951CC79C9A2DCC1A60 has outputs[0] = that exact coin, 100000000, in block 8
rejection was raised at 12:23:49Z, before block 8 existed on the node
enabling node automine before the run does not help: the check still happens before the post is processed

reproduced unchanged on Hawk v0.3.0 (built from release/0.3.0 @985b859, LMDB+DuckDB): channel 0xe6863650602f6f7a3e1b99df1ebba8d1 rejected coin 0x823afc4cabe74c109c2b1b794d16aec2e0a2362b4b5816d209d62d701065a6d0
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts: submitOpenChannel posts, then requestPeerReply(CHANNEL_PROPOSAL, 20s)
packages/omnia/src/channel.ts: acceptChannel resolves the funding coin from the chain provider and throws when absent

fix.approach: Make the handshake tolerate the inclusion delay instead of assuming it away. On the initiator, wait for the funding coin to be observable through the chain provider (bounded, with a named timeout) before sending CHANNEL_PROPOSAL; on the responder, treat "coin not yet found" as retryable for a bounded window rather than an immediate terminal rejection. Either side alone fixes the common case; doing both covers a slow block and a fast initiator.
constraints: Do not remove the on-chain funding-coin check: it is what stops an unfunded channel from being accepted.
Do not raise the existing 20s peer-reply timeout as the mechanism; the wait belongs around chain inclusion.
Do not add an unbounded wait or a sleep-and-hope; bound it and fail with the observed height and coin id.
acceptance: A open against a live node succeeds when the funding tx is mined a few seconds after submission.
An open whose funding tx is never mined fails within a bounded time with a message naming the coin and the chain height.
The responder still rejects a proposal whose funding coin does not exist (no regression in the safety check).
Offline and in-memory suites still pass.
